title: Setups to research

stories.title: Bullish consensus on AMZN
stories.summary: The feed's optimism rests on AWS speeding up (39% growth in Q3), new retail areas (Amazon Autos opening in the UK in early 2027) and reported talks with Meta over access for its Muse AI shopping agent.

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: The feed's optimism rests on AWS speeding up (39% growth in Q3), new retail areas (Amazon Autos opening in the UK in early 2027) and reported talks with Meta over access for its Muse AI shopping agent. Shares rebounded to the mid-$260s after the midterms, about 6% below the August high of roughly $284. That suggests some of the AWS story is priced in, but worries about AI capex still cap the multiple.

cards.title: Findings · 1/3
items: Q3 2026 (Oct 29): revenue about $201.9B and AWS growth of 39%, its fastest in years. The stock first fell on concerns about AI spending.

Fortune reported on Nov 25 that Amazon and Meta have held several rounds of talks on restoring Muse's access to Amazon.com, blocked since Sept 20. Advertising and search placement are the sticking points, both CEOs would have to sign off, and a deal is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Findings · 2/3
items: Amazon Autos launches in the UK in early 2027, with Hyundai as the first brand and Vertu Motors for used cars. Buyers reserve online and complete the purchase at a dealer, so the near-term revenue impact is small.
Live sports on Prime Video (NFL, NBA) feed first-party customer data and ad inventory, which supports the advertising growth story.

cards.title: Findings · 3/3
items: Consensus is 'Strong Buy' with an average target of about $332, roughly 25% above mid-November levels. Insiders sold heavily after Q2, including about $4.5B from CEO Andy Jassy.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: Any Amazon–Meta Muse agreement and its terms on ads and search: shows whether Amazon can make money from third-party AI agents or loses ad traffic to them
Black Friday / Cyber Monday (Nov 27–30) and holiday-quarter retail read-throughs
AWS re:Invent (early December): AI chip (Trainium) and agent announcements, plus updates on the Anthropic stake after ANT's IPO

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: Q4 2026 earnings (late Jan/early Feb 2027, not yet announced): AWS growth rate and 2027 capex guidance

cards.title: Risks
items: Capex intensity: rising AI infrastructure spending could squeeze free cash flow, and markets have punished that before
AI shopping agents (Muse, ChatGPT, Claude) could route around Amazon's high-margin ad business, and Amazon has blocked them so far
Heavy insider selling, plus a stock already near its highs after the election rally, leaves less room if holiday or AWS numbers disappoint

stories.title: Bullish consensus on SPCX
stories.summary: The feed is excited about the FCC's Nov 25 authorization for up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites and Musk's 'two shares for every child' post.

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: The feed is excited about the FCC's Nov 25 authorization for up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites and Musk's 'two shares for every child' post. The stock barely reacted: it fell as much as about 10% intraday, then closed up about 1.3% near $127.44, still below its $135 June IPO price. The orbital data-center plan looks like a long-dated option already in the valuation, and the Dec 8 lockup expiry is the nearer-term driver.

cards.title: Findings · 1/2
items: The FCC approved the 'Starmind' plan for up to 1M orbital data-center satellites. Build-out milestones reportedly start with a first operational satellite by Nov 2033 and half the constellation by 2038. SpaceX's prospectus suggests initial compute satellites as early as 2028.
On approval day the stock sold off with the wider tech market, then recovered, a sign the news was expected since the January filing.

cards.title: Findings · 2/2
items: SPCX has traded below its $135 IPO price (June 11, 2026) since approval. The IPO raised roughly $75–86B, with reported figures varying.
Musk's post that every American child would get two SpaceX shares is a sentiment driver. Its mechanics, cost and legal path are unclear, and it is not a company-filed program.
Skeptics such as Forrester put hardware costs alone at $250B to $1T before launch and refresh, so the economics are unproven.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: Dec 8, 2026 lockup expiry: hundreds of millions more shares become eligible for sale
$135 IPO price as resistance and about $114 (the Nov 25 intraday low) as support
News on a possible Tesla/xAI combination, which has weighed on the stock

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: Starship launch cadence and Starlink subscriber/revenue updates

cards.title: Risks
items: Lockup supply on Dec 8 and the stock trading below its IPO price both create overhang
Governance and related-party risk from Musk-linked entities (xAI, Tesla merger talk)
Orbital compute faces huge capital needs, unproven unit economics and timelines that run into the 2030s

stories.title: Bullish consensus on ANT
stories.summary: Anthropic priced a record IPO at $83 on Nov 19 (above its $70–78 range), opened at $111.50 and peaked near $115.

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: Anthropic priced a record IPO at $83 on Nov 19 (above its $70–78 range), opened at $111.50 and peaked near $115. A week-long tech sell-off then pushed it briefly below the IPO price. It is now around $83.50, roughly $1T in market value. The bullish case is about stabilization and valuation versus peers: analysts at William Blair and Wedbush rate it Outperform (Wedbush target $120), and the FY27 revenue estimate cited is about $136.5B. Bears point to AI spending commitments and lockup supply.

cards.title: Findings · 1/3
items: The IPO raised a record of about $107B, larger than SpaceX's. First-day close was $97.17, with reported valuations ranging from $1.27T to $1.76T depending on share count.

Shares are down more than 30% from the first-day peak of $115.10. CNBC (Nov 25) reports the stock settling near a $1T market cap, and analysts argue its enterprise customer base makes it steadier than other AI names.

cards.title: Findings · 2/3
items: Valuation framing in the feed: about $136.5B of FY27 revenue estimated, with peers above 8x sales. That implies upside if those estimates hold, but the revenue figure is a forward estimate, not reported results.
Options sellers are pitching covered-call or yield products (e.g. YANT) as lower-risk exposure, a sign that implied volatility is high.

cards.title: Findings · 3/3
items: Lockup terms are unusual: the prospectus reportedly lists 23 staged earnings- and time-based release events, and about 40% of the deal was reportedly freed on day one.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: Around Dec 14, 2026: the 25-day quiet period ends and underwriter analyst coverage begins
Possible Russell 1000 inclusion after the close on Dec 11, 2026, subject to confirmation
$83 IPO price as the key support/sentiment line, and the $97–115 first-day range above

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: First quarterly report as a public company (date not yet confirmed) and the next staged lockup release

cards.title: Risks
items: Reported spending commitments of about $900B on compute weigh on margins and cash flow
Staged lockup releases add steady supply of shares
The stock is highly correlated with AI and tech sentiment, so a sector sell-off could keep it below the IPO price

stories.title: CRWV under pressure
stories.summary: CoreWeave's selloff comes mainly from its credit.

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: CoreWeave's selloff comes mainly from its credit. Five-year CDS hit records around Nov 25 (about 1,314bp per one report, an intraday 1,534bp per another), its 9% 2031 bonds fell to the mid-70s cents (roughly 17-18% yield), and banks are trying to sell a new Meta-backed GPU loan into a market that has gone cold on AI data center debt. Bulls point to a backlog of about $132.5B and contract-secured financing. Bears point to heavy capex against revenue and dependence on credit markets staying open. Price swings are large in both directions: one report has the stock closing nearly flat on Nov 25 after a 10%+ intraday drop.

cards.title: Findings · 1/4
items: Record credit stress: five-year CDS at about 1,314bp on Nov 25, which S&P Global Market Intelligence's model reads as roughly a 68% five-year default probability (another report has an intraday 1,534bp and over 70%). The 2031 9% notes hit 76.6 cents, their lowest since issue.

cards.title: Findings · 2/4
items: Loan sale: Bloomberg reported on Nov 11 that Morgan Stanley and MUFG are arranging an investment-grade loan of at least $4B secured by GPUs and the Meta contract, to be marketed to other lenders. The feed says $4.5B to be sold next week; I found no reporting of that exact figure. The CFO guided a 7-7.5% yield on the next contract-backed loan.

cards.title: Findings · 3/4
items: The stock fell about 13% the previous day and kept falling Nov 25. Reports differ: one says it was down 10.27% at $38.23 early in the session, another says it closed near flat at $42.57. It is down roughly 47% year to date and fell about 36% in October alone.

cards.title: Findings · 4/4
items: Sector contagion: CDS on other AI names (Oracle, and per some reports Nvidia and Google) widened. Banks are using secondary loan sales and significant risk transfers to cut their exposure to AI and data center debt.

Bull counterpoint: much of the debt is backed by contracts with investment-grade customers (Meta) and the backlog is about $132.5B. Some analysts say CDS this wide may partly reflect hedging rather than a change in the business.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: Syndication of the Meta-backed GPU loan (marketing reportedly from the week of Nov 16 or later): final pricing against the 7-7.5% guide and the size of the order book
CDS near 1,300-1,500bp and the 2031 bond price near 76 cents: further widening or a stabilization
The intraday low near $38 from Nov 25 as a level for a washout or a break

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: Other AI credit: Oracle and Nvidia CDS, plus any loan sales or risk transfers on other data center projects

cards.title: Risks
items: Bear-case risk: if loan syndication fails or is repriced wider, refinancing costs rise and capex plans may have to shrink, deepening the stock's slide
Bull-case risk: with deeply discounted debt and record CDS, a successful loan placement or any easing in AI credit could set off a sharp short-covering reversal
The data is inconsistent: CDS levels, bond yields and closing prices differ across outlets, so verify on Bloomberg or CNBC

stories.title: OPENAI under pressure
stories.summary: OpenAI is private, so the negative tone shows up through proxies: prediction markets pushing the expected IPO into 2027, weaker odds on its valuation, and stress across the AI financing chain (SoftBank, Nvidia's Ports-Pi

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: OpenAI is private, so the negative tone shows up through proxies: prediction markets pushing the expected IPO into 2027, weaker odds on its valuation, and stress across the AI financing chain (SoftBank, Nvidia's Ports-Pike backstop, banks cutting their exposure to data center loans). On the other side, Brockman says the company could be IPO-ready in 2027, enterprise revenue is reportedly growing, and new products such as Private Inference are in testing. There is no clean washout signal. Sentiment depends on the AI credit cycle more than on OpenAI's own operations.

cards.title: Findings · 1/3
items: IPO timing: prediction markets now put most of the probability on a 2027 IPO (one snapshot had about 80% for after Jan 1, 2027). One market on OpenAI's valuation fell from about 80% to just above 50% after the delay. Reports mention a confidential S-1 and a 2027 target.
Its last private round was $122B at an $852B post-money valuation (March 2026). Anthropic is expected to list first, which could set the benchmark for comparisons.

cards.title: Findings · 2/3
items: Financing chain: Nvidia confirmed it is backing 4.25GW of OpenAI capacity at SoftBank's Ports-Pike (Portsmouth, Ohio) site, but only for defined portions of lease and power payments and a residual-value commitment, which is narrower than the headline $105B. The feed's Cramer item ties Nvidia's weakness to this exposure.

cards.title: Findings · 3/3
items: Banks (JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, SMBC, MUFG) have explored loan sales and significant risk transfers on AI data center debt and are tightening lending standards. That raises the cost of capital for OpenAI's compute buildout.
Product side: Altman says OpenAI Private Inference, part of OpenAI Private Intelligence, is being tested with a small group of customers, which fits the shift toward enterprise revenue.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: IPO odds on Polymarket and Kalshi, and any public S-1 or IPO timing news
Anthropic's IPO timing and valuation as a read-through for OpenAI
AI credit gauges: CoreWeave and Oracle CDS, bank loan sales tied to OpenAI or SoftBank data center projects

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: SoftBank and Nvidia statements on Ports-Pike financing; Nvidia's next earnings

cards.title: Risks
items: Bear-case risk: a sustained shutdown of AI credit could force cuts to compute commitments and a down-round or a further IPO delay
Bull-case risk: stronger enterprise revenue, product launches, or an Anthropic IPO that prices well could quickly lift sentiment and IPO odds
Prediction-market odds are thin and quickly go stale, and much of the coverage comes from secondary or crypto outlets

stories.title: GC under pressure
stories.summary: Gold's slide is driven by expectations of Fed rate hikes.

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: Gold's slide is driven by expectations of Fed rate hikes. October PCE inflation came in at 3.8% and Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%, and a firmer dollar adds pressure, taking bullion down about 36% from its Jan 28 record of $5,589. It broke below $3,500 on Wednesday for the first time since Sept 2025, then steadied around $3,560 on Thursday, Nov 26. That rebound fits a possible washout, but the macro backdrop is still bearish until rate-hike expectations fade.

cards.title: Findings · 1/3
items: Macro driver: hot inflation (October PCE at 3.8%) and strong growth (Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%) keep Fed hikes on the table, pushing real yields and the dollar higher, both headwinds for gold.
Price path: spot gold fell to about $3,881 on Nov 12 (a one-year low), hit a 14-month low on Nov 19, and briefly broke $3,500 on Nov 25. The feed's $3,432 print is the low end of that intraday move.

cards.title: Findings · 2/3
items: Possible washout: CNBC reports gold steadying on Nov 26 after the over-one-year low, with Kitco showing about $3,564 at 7:55 a.m. ET, a quick recovery back above $3,500.

Analysts see $3,400-3,500 as the key support zone. GoldInvest says only a sustained break below it would change the longer-term picture, and some commentators would treat $3,500 as a long-term buying level.

cards.title: Findings · 3/3
items: The bear case has its own targets: some firms forecast $3,500 or lower into 2027, and earlier the oil-driven inflation fears tied to fading Middle East peace hopes hit gold rather than lifting it.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: $3,500 and the $3,400-3,500 support zone: a weekly close below it versus a quick recapture; resistance near $3,595 and $3,880-3,900
December FOMC meeting (mid-Dec 2026) and the Fed speakers before it on a possible hike
November jobs report (early Dec) and November CPI (mid-Dec)

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: Dollar index and real yields; central bank and ETF gold flows

cards.title: Risks
items: Bear-case risk: a dovish Fed surprise, softer data, or a geopolitical or credit shock (for example, AI debt stress spreading) could revive safe-haven demand and trigger a sharp short-covering rally
Bull-case risk: an actual Fed hike plus a stronger dollar could bring a sustained break below $3,400 and forced liquidation from leveraged longs
Holiday-thin Thanksgiving trading can exaggerate moves and produce false breaks

stories.title: Shift in market mood
stories.summary: The slide in feed sentiment from -25 to -100 matches a rough Wednesday, Nov 25 session.

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: The slide in feed sentiment from -25 to -100 matches a rough Wednesday, Nov 25 session. A renewed AI and chip sell-off (Nvidia was down more than 9% intraday and closed about -3.9%) hit at the same time as newly proposed tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other partners, plus hot October PCE inflation of about 3.8% y/y. Reports disagree on how bad the close was: Reuters-based wires cited a Nasdaq drop of about 4%, while Yahoo's close report shows indexes recovering much of the loss. That suggests the panic was sharper intraday than at the close.

cards.title: Findings · 1/4
items: Tariffs: the administration proposed duties of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other major partners, aimed at excess industrial capacity, to take effect next year. This comes even though the Supreme Court ruled earlier this year that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, so other legal authorities are presumably being used. Because the start date is next year, there is room for negotiated deals, which the feed links to lower rates.

cards.title: Findings · 2/4
items: AI and semis: Nvidia's Monday rally on Jensen Huang's reported return as CEO faded. NVDA closed about -3.9% Wednesday after being down more than 9% intraday. Reports tying Trump to Nvidia shares and a possible Huang pardon add political and headline risk. I could not confirm the details of a formal 'government stake' proposal.

cards.title: Findings · 3/4
items: Inflation: October PCE was reported at about 3.8% y/y. CPI has risen more than expected for three straight months (September CPI 3.7%, with October estimated at 3.9–4.0%), which limits how much the Fed can ease.
Index backdrop: the S&P 500 was reported down about 5.2–5.5% for November going into the holiday, so sentiment was already fragile before Wednesday.

cards.title: Findings · 4/4
items: Cross-asset: crypto weakness (BTC down roughly 26% from its peak, a stablecoin supply contraction, ETF outflows) adds to the risk-off tone, while the 'bond optimism' in the feed fits a flight to Treasuries.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: Nov 27: half-day US session after Thanksgiving; thin liquidity can exaggerate moves
Dec 1: Nvidia GTC DC keynote (date per the feed, not independently verified), a possible AI sentiment catalyst
Dec 4: November jobs report (per a third-party preview); Dec 8–9: FOMC with the decision and SEP Dec 9 at 2:00pm ET; Dec 10: November CPI

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: Tariff negotiations with the 14 named partners before the proposed duties take effect next year; any deal headlines

cards.title: Risks · 1/2
items: Upside risk to the bearish mood: an extreme reading like -100 often comes near short-term washouts, and Wednesday's intraday recovery shows dip buyers are still active. A strong GTC, tariff deals or a softer CPI could spark a sharp relief rally.
Downside: sticky inflation near 4% plus new tariffs could lead the Fed to hold or turn hawkish on Dec 9, which would pressure richly valued AI and semiconductor names further.

cards.title: Risks · 2/2
items: Data quality: coverage of Wednesday's close conflicts (Nasdaq -4% vs about -0.6%), and some Nvidia/Huang/Trump headlines are unusual and thinly sourced. Confirm them before relying on them.

stories.title: Main risks flagged today
stories.summary: The bearish posts flag three linked risks: renewed tariffs at a time of rising inflation (a stagflation-type squeeze on Fed policy), an unfinished AI and semiconductor correction, and a crypto liquidity drain shown by sh

cards.title: Summary
cards.text: The bearish posts flag three linked risks: renewed tariffs at a time of rising inflation (a stagflation-type squeeze on Fed policy), an unfinished AI and semiconductor correction, and a crypto liquidity drain shown by shrinking stablecoin supply and spot ETF outflows. Each has real evidence behind it. The tariffs are proposals that could still be negotiated, and several sentiment gauges are at extremes that have historically come near short-term lows.

cards.title: Findings · 1/4
items: Inflation plus tariffs: CPI has run above expectations for three straight months (about 3.7% in September, October estimated at 3.9–4.0%) and October PCE is about 3.8%. The newly proposed duties of up to 20% on 14 partners could add goods inflation next year. This is probably the most serious risk because it limits Fed easing.

cards.title: Findings · 2/4
items: Semiconductors: SentimenTrader says it is too soon to call a bottom, and Nvidia's 9% intraday drop on Nov 25 showed that rebounds are still being sold. With tech sentiment at 14, positioning is already washed out, though, which works against the bear case.

cards.title: Findings · 3/4
items: Crypto: 21Shares says stablecoin supply fell about $10.7B in 18 days after the Binance hack, the biggest drop since Terra in 2022. Spot BTC and ETH ETFs saw roughly $3.9B of combined outflows. 21Shares names BTC's realized price of about $53,250 as the key downside level and views $37.2K–$43.8K as unlikely for now.

cards.title: Findings · 4/4
items: Scale: total stablecoin supply is still only about 8% below its May record, and the steepest leg of the BTC decline came from forced deleveraging, which tends to be self-limiting. The crypto risk is serious for that asset class but less clearly systemic.

cards.title: Watch · 1/2
items: BTC realized price near $53,250 as the downside level 21Shares flags; daily spot ETF flow prints and the stablecoin supply trend
Dec 4 jobs report and Dec 10 November CPI, which bracket the FOMC decision on Dec 9
Dec 1 Nvidia GTC DC keynote (per the feed) as a test of whether the AI sell-off stabilizes

cards.title: Watch · 2/2
items: Partner responses or retaliation to the proposed tariffs, and any legal challenge after the IEEPA ruling

cards.title: Risks · 1/2
items: Risk to the bearish view: crowded pessimism (tech sentiment at 14, feed mood at -100) and negotiable, delayed tariffs could set up a sharp rebound and squeeze shorts.
Risk that the bears are underestimating: if inflation near 4% forces the Fed to signal no cuts or a hike at its SEP meeting, the equity, semiconductor and crypto drawdowns could compound together.

cards.title: Risks · 2/2
items: Contagion: a further Binance or exchange-related stress event, or continued ETF redemptions, could push BTC below its realized price and spill into risk sentiment more broadly.
